title: The CFA Franc: 14 African Countries, One Euro Peg, and the Eco Plan | The Six, Ep. 2
lede: Fourteen African countries use a currency fixed at 655.957 to the euro since 1999, backed by a French Treasury guarantee. A 2019 reform ended West Africa's reserve deposits in Paris, but the peg, the guarantee and the name are unchanged. This episode explains how the two CFA francs work, what the reform did, and where the eco stands.
keyPoints: Two currencies: the West African CFA franc (8 WAEMU countries, BCEAO) and the Central African CFA franc (6 CEMAC countries, BEAC), both fixed at €1 = 655.957.

The December 2019 reform closed the BCEAO's operations account at the French Treasury and removed France from its governing bodies. The euro peg and French guarantee remain, and the rename to the eco has not happened.
Mali, Burkina Faso and Niger left ECOWAS in January 2025 but remain in the West African monetary union and still use the CFA franc.
ECOWAS reaffirmed a 2027 launch of its own eco on July 19, 2026, starting with countries that meet convergence criteria.
The BRVM, the eight-country exchange in Abidjan, was worth almost 21 trillion CFA francs on Nov. 2, 2026, up from about 13.3 trillion at the end of 2025.
